item.title: Brewing WordPress Passion
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
Sharing the Love of WordPress:

I’m a self-proclaimed ‘coffee-loving WordPress nerd’ with a passion for helping others learn WordPress. Currently, I am part of the LevelUp Core Operations Team, and leading the training and development, where I enjoy sharing my knowledge about WordPress with my other colleagues. I love sharing my knowledge about WordPress with others.

Throughout my career, I’ve built beautiful, functional websites for small businesses, focusing on conversion optimization using WordPress. I also love helping fellow WordPress users resolve their technical issues, and sharing my enthusiasm and expertise to make their WordPress journey smoother.

Sharing my love for WordPress is more than just a job for me—it’s about empowering others to succeed.

My WordPress Journey:

I started using WordPress in college around 2012 and became an active contributor in 2015. My initial contribution revolved around providing assistance to others in the forums and addressing technical support inquiries. This spark made me want to get involved more and explore other teams like Polyglots, Photos, Training, and of course, the Community. This spirit of connection extended to the Philippine WordPress local meetups, where I actively contributed to organizing events in my hometown and surrounding areas.

Building a Bigger Table with WordCamp Asia:

WordCamps, both local and flagship events like WordCamp Asia, always draw me in. The first time I attended WordCamp Asia was in Bangkok in 2023, and the next year I volunteered at WordCamp Asia 2024 in Taipei. This time, I joined the organizing team for WordCamp Asia 2025. 

As part of the Contributor Day organizing team, I am organizing a special day dedicated to collaboration on contributing to improve the WordPress project, such as in areas such as code, design, documentation, etc. My primary focus is Contributor Day, but I also actively support other teams whenever possible, especially the local and venue team tasks.

Reflecting on the Past and Embracing the Future:

My decision to join the WordCamp Asia organizing team was based on my deep love for the WordPress community and a desire to contribute on a larger scale. Volunteering at the WordCamp Asia 2024 showed me how these events help people work together and make connections. 

As an organizer, my mission is to create an environment where attendees can learn, connect, and grow. It’s a chance to give back to the community that has given me so much. With growing excitement and anticipation for WordCamp Asia 2025, I envision a diverse gathering fostering learning, innovation, and a vibrant exchange of ideas. 

My role as an organizer is to create a welcoming and productive environment, particularly during Contributor Day, where we can inspire new contributors and strengthen the global WordPress community. Ultimately, I’m driven to make this a memorable and impactful experience for everyone involved.

item.title: Building a Christ-Centered Relationship Starts with the Right Mindset
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
As followers of Christ, relationships are not just about companionship or personal fulfillment—they are an opportunity to reflect God’s love and purpose. Before pursuing someone you admire, it’s essential to examine your heart and align your intentions with God’s will. A Christ-centered relationship requires a mindset rooted in faith, selflessness, and a desire to glorify God together.

1. Reflect on Your Intentions – A Mindset of Flourishing in Christ
Ask yourself: Why do I want to be in this relationship? If your motivation is solely for personal gain—such as avoiding loneliness or fulfilling selfish desires—then your foundation may not be strong enough to sustain a God-honoring relationship.

Instead, reflect on how your relationship can reflect Christ’s love. Consider this mindset: “I want to help this person flourish spiritually, emotionally, and relationally, so they can grow closer to Christ and live out their God-given purpose.” The Bible reminds us in Philippians 2:3-4 to “do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves, not looking to your own interests but each of you to the interests of the others.” A relationship built on this principle creates a foundation of mutual respect and love under God’s guidance.

2. Evaluate Your Commitment – A Mindset of Wholehearted Surrender
Entering a relationship requires not only excitement but also a deep commitment to God’s plan for you and your partner. Luke 14:28 reminds us to “count the cost” in all things. Before starting a relationship, ask yourself: Am I ready to honor God through this journey?

Be prepared to grow in areas such as:

  1. Surrendering your own flaws to God and seeking His strength to improve.
  2. Investing time in building a Christ-centered connection.
  3. Being patient, loving, and understanding even during difficult seasons.
  4. Supporting your partner in their faith journey.

If you’re ready to make Christ the center of your relationship and commit to His plan, then proceed with prayer, clarity, and purpose.

3. Consider the Impact – A Mindset of Adding Godly Value
Sometimes, the idea of pursuing someone can be intimidating, especially if they seem accomplished or spiritually mature. Instead of focusing on your inadequacies, focus on how you can serve and encourage them in their walk with Christ.

Ask yourself: Can I commit to being a godly influence and source of encouragement in their life? If your answer is, “With God’s help, I will love, protect, and encourage them to grow in their faith and fulfill their God-given calling,” then you’re approaching the relationship with the right heart.

A relationship that honors God requires humility and confidence in His purpose for you both. Colossians 3:14 reminds us, “And over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity.” This love is selfless, sacrificial, and rooted in a commitment to God’s design for relationships.

A Final Thought
Pursuing a meaningful connection begins with putting Christ at the center of your intentions, commitment, and actions. Seek God’s guidance through prayer and Scripture, and be willing to grow in your faith as you prepare to share your journey with someone else. If you’re ready to honor God through selflessness and love, step forward with confidence, trusting Him to guide your steps.

“Commit to the Lord whatever you do, and He will establish your plans.” (Proverbs 16:3)

item.title: Leadership of a Lion
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
What is a Leader?

Leaders are unique individuals with a distinct mindset that sets them apart from followers. If you aspire to be an impactful personality, you must change how you see yourself and the world.

The Nature and Attitude of the Lion

A lion is recognized as the leader or king of the jungle, not because he is the tallest, largest, or smartest, but because of his unwavering attitude. The lion’s belief in his dominance makes him fearless, earning him respect from every other animal. Likewise, leadership doesn’t require you to have special advantages; it’s your belief and attitude that truly matter.

Our thoughts shape us into leaders or followers. Leadership is an attitude, a product of our beliefs. The lion sees himself as king—and so he is. Similarly, the elephant, though physically stronger, feels inferior in the presence of the lion due to his belief system. Your mindset ultimately shapes your life, and no amount of skill can replace the power of the right attitude.

Developing Leadership: 3 Key Factors

Your journey to becoming a leader depends on:

  • Your perception of who you are
  • Why you believe you exist
  • Your sense of significance

Find your purpose, embrace a leadership mindset, and walk boldly through life. Leadership demands that you elevate your attitude, develop your gifts, and surround yourself with people who inspire you. Remember, true leaders empower others, nurturing leadership potential in those around them.

"When you discover leadership, it comes out in your attitude."

Two Aspects of Leadership

1. The Leadership Spirit:
We are all born with the potential to lead, though our environment may stifle it. To lead, you must break free from societal expectations and courageously carve your own path, even if it means leaving certain friendships or norms behind.

2. The Spirit of Leadership:
This refers to a leader’s attitude and mindset. It is the self-belief that drives you, influences your perception of the world, and strengthens your conviction to lead.

7 Principles of True Leadership

  1. Inherent Capacity: Leadership is within everyone. Dying as a follower is a choice.
  2. Self-Discovery: True leadership cannot be taught; it must be found within.
  3. Self-Understanding: Great leadership is about knowing yourself.
  4. Service: Leadership is serving your unique gifts to the world.
  5. Self-Assessment: Regularly reflect on your strengths and growth areas.
  6. Manifesting Potential: Real leadership emerges when you act beyond what others can pay you for; it requires bearing risks.
  7. Self-Exposure: Live fully, serving the world with your gifts.

“You must decide if you are going to rob the world or bless it with the rich, valuable, potent, untapped resources locked away within you.”
— Dr. Myles Munroe

The Five Questions of Life

  1. Who am I? – Understand your destiny.
  2. Where am I from? – Know your heritage; we are citizens of heaven.
  3. Why am I here? – Discover your purpose.
  4. What can I do? – Identify your gifts, talents, and skills.
  5. Where am I going? – Uncover your destiny.

Welcome to my corner of the web! I’m Jhimross Olinares—a coffee-loving WordPress enthusiast with a passion for helping others master WordPress and a love for sharing my experiences along the way.

Starting this blog felt like the natural next step in my journey. Through my work with WordPress, Quality Assurance, and representing LevelUp on the global stage, I’ve discovered a deep drive to help others succeed. This blog is a space where I can share insights, tips, and personal reflections on topics that have shaped who I am.

Beyond the technical aspects of WordPress, I’m here to share a bit of what fuels me outside of work. I love the thrill of cycling, the competitive yet fulfilling nature of badminton, and the endless journey of self-development. I believe that personal growth and continuous learning are as crucial in life as in any professional setting. And underpinning all these passions is my faith in Jesus, which gives me purpose, resilience, and joy in everything I do.

Through this blog, I hope to connect with like-minded people, share practical insights, and hopefully inspire you to pursue your own passions. Whether it’s mastering WordPress, achieving personal goals, or exploring spiritual growth, I’m excited to share this journey with you. Here’s to learning, growing, and sharing—together.

item.title: The Power of Your Attitude
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
"Attitude, not aptitude, determines your altitude." – John Maxwell

Our attitude shapes so much more of our lives than we might initially think. Here’s how cultivating a positive, proactive attitude can deeply impact both your personal and professional life.

1. Your Attitude Reveals Who You Are

Your attitude stems from the core of who you are—it’s a reflection of your inner self. As Proverbs 23:7 reminds us, "As a man thinketh in his heart, so is he." Attitude often expresses itself through our actions or reactions, speaking much louder than the words we say. People around us constantly interpret our true selves through our attitudes, especially during challenging situations. When life presents difficulties, our attitude often shows our true colors, revealing who we really are.

2. Your Attitude Determines the Success and Failure of Every Relationship

Every relationship in our life is influenced by our attitude. A positive attitude can foster closeness, understanding, and growth, while a negative one can create friction and distance. A bad attitude can be especially destructive, eventually spilling out in harmful words and actions that can damage trust and goodwill. When someone harbors a poor attitude, it’s only a matter of time before it impacts those around them. Thus, cultivating a positive outlook is essential for building and maintaining healthy relationships.

3. Your Attitude is Always Your Choice

While we can’t control what happens to us each day, we do have the power to choose our response. We may not be able to dictate every circumstance, but we can control our attitude toward it. Understanding this power is key to personal growth, resilience, and fulfillment. Every day, we have the chance to choose a constructive attitude—one that will serve us, rather than hinder us.

Steps to Help You Cultivate a Positive Attitude:

  1. Speak Positive Words: Begin each day by affirming the good, focusing on what you are grateful for.
  2. Seek the Good in All Situations: No matter what life throws your way, look for the silver lining—you’ll find it.
  3. Take Charge of Your Thoughts:
    • Fix your mind on positive, constructive ideas.
    • Filter out negativity that doesn’t serve you.
    • Feed your mind with uplifting content and messages that inspire growth.

Embracing a positive attitude not only transforms your outlook on life but can also uplift those around you. Remember, your attitude is a choice—one that holds the power to elevate your life to new heights.

item.title: In the Middle of the Storm
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
Storms have a way of disrupting life—leaving behind destruction, fear, and uncertainty. While news headlines often highlight natural disasters, there are other storms just as devastating: sickness, financial hardship, and broken relationships. These personal storms threaten our peace, comfort, and joy, leaving us vulnerable to fear, doubt, and hopelessness.

In Mark 4:35–41, we see the disciples caught in a storm, both physical and spiritual, while crossing the Sea of Galilee. The wind and waves raged against their small boat, and fear consumed them. Meanwhile, Jesus was asleep in the stern. Overwhelmed, they cried out, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?” (Mark 4:38).

Jesus awoke, rebuked the wind and sea with the words, “Peace! Be still!” (Mark 4:39), and questioned their faith. Stunned, the disciples were no longer afraid of the storm but marveled at Jesus’ authority over nature, asking, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” (Mark 4:41).

The disciples learned powerful lessons that day—lessons we can apply as we face our own storms.

God Ordains the Storms of Life

It’s hard to accept that a loving God permits trials in our lives. For some, it seems contradictory: “If God loves me, why does He allow suffering?” But Jesus Himself addressed this tension:

"In this world you will have tribulation. But take heart; I have overcome the world.” (John 16:33)

Jesus promised we would face difficulties, but He also reassured us of His victory over them. Trials test the genuineness of our faith, as James 1:2-3 reminds us:

"Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.”

In Mark 4, the disciples’ faith was tested. They doubted Jesus’ care for them in their fear, asking if He even cared that they were in danger. We often feel the same way when faced with health crises or financial struggles, but Scripture reminds us to cast our cares on Him because He cares deeply for us (1 Peter 5:7).

God Is in Control of the Storms

When Jesus calmed the storm, He demonstrated His absolute sovereignty. He is not merely present during our trials—He has control over them. As Psalm 24:1-2 proclaims:

"The earth is the LORD’s, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it; for he founded it on the seas and established it on the waters.”

This sovereignty assures us that nothing happens outside God’s plan or power. While the disciples were right to turn to Jesus in the storm, they did so in fear and doubt rather than faith. Instead, Jesus calls us to trust Him completely. Philippians 4:6-7 offers the key:

"Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.”

When we thank God for His power and purpose in the storm, His peace guards us from fear and anxiety.

God Is for You in the Storm

In their fear, the disciples questioned Jesus’ care for them. Jesus rebuked both the storm and their unbelief, reminding them of His deep love and faithfulness.

Isaiah 41:10 reassures us:

"Fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.”

Believing that God is for you changes everything. When trials come, you won’t be tempted to doubt His love or purpose. Even when He seems silent, you can trust His promises.

Trusting God in the Storm

The storms of life are part of God’s sanctification process. They reveal our hearts, refine our faith, and draw us closer to Him. Isaiah 43:2 promises:

"When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you."

Let the storms of life remind you of God’s faithfulness. Instead of focusing on the size of the storm, focus on the greatness of God. He is your refuge, deliverer, and peace in every trial.

Trust Him, for He has overcome the world.

item.title: The Journey Behind My Love for Cycling
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
Cycling has always been more than just a mode of transportation for me. It’s been a transformative journey—one that has shaped my body, mind, and spirit. From the first time I hopped on a bike to the countless rides I've taken since, cycling has become an essential part of my life. But beyond the thrill of the ride and the joy of exploring new paths, there’s a deeper connection for me—one rooted in personal growth and faith.

Why I Cycle? The Freedom of the Open Road

So, why do I cycle? It’s a question I’ve often reflected on during my rides. The simple answer is that cycling gives me a sense of freedom that few other activities do. There’s something special about feeling the wind against your face and the road beneath your wheels, knowing that every pedal stroke takes you one step closer to where you want to go.

But beyond the physical thrill, cycling allows me to connect with myself in a way that few other things can. It’s a space where I can reflect, pray, and clear my mind. The rhythm of the pedaling, the beauty of the landscapes, and the silence of the open road make it an ideal setting for introspection and personal growth.

Cycling as a Form of Self-Development

Cycling isn’t just a way to stay fit—it’s a way to challenge myself and push my limits. Every ride is an opportunity to grow, whether it’s testing my endurance on a long-distance ride or overcoming obstacles like steep hills or tough weather conditions. There have been countless moments where I’ve wanted to give up, but something inside me keeps pushing forward.

Each time I overcome a challenge, it strengthens my belief that I am capable of more than I often realize. It’s a reminder that self-development is a journey, and sometimes, the hardest challenges bring the most growth.

Cycling has also taught me the importance of setting goals. Whether it’s completing a certain distance or improving my average speed, the sense of accomplishment I feel after achieving these goals is deeply satisfying. These small victories in cycling spill over into other areas of my life, where I continue to set and achieve personal goals—whether in my career, faith, or relationships.

Cycling Adventures and Challenges

Every cycling adventure has a story to tell. I’ve ridden through busy city streets, quiet country roads, and scenic mountain paths. Each route holds its own set of challenges, but it’s those challenges that make the journey worthwhile.

One of the most memorable moments in my cycling journey was a solo ride through a mountain trail I had never attempted before. The path was steep and rugged, and there were times when I wasn’t sure if I would make it to the top. But as I reached the summit, the view that awaited me was nothing short of breathtaking. That feeling of accomplishment—of conquering something that seemed impossible—was one I’ll never forget.

I’ve had my fair share of flat tires, unexpected rainstorms, and sore muscles, but every challenge has only made me more resilient. The key, I’ve learned, is to keep moving forward. No matter how tough the ride, there’s always something rewarding waiting on the other side.

Faith and Cycling: Finding Clarity on the Road

Cycling has also become a space for me to nurture my faith. There’s something about being on the road, surrounded by nature, that makes it easier to reflect and connect with God. I often find myself praying during long rides, asking for guidance or simply thanking Him for the strength to keep going.

Cycling offers me a unique opportunity for solitude and peace—time to listen to God and hear His voice. It's in these quiet moments that I often find clarity for the challenges I face in life. My rides are not just physical exercises; they are moments of spiritual renewal and reflection.

Cycling Tips and Gear Reviews

If you’re considering starting your own cycling journey, here are a few tips to help you get started:

  1. Start Small – Don’t feel pressured to go on long rides right away. Start with short, easy routes and gradually build up your stamina.
  2. Comfort is Key – Invest in a comfortable bike seat and padded shorts. Trust me, your body will thank you!
  3. Stay Hydrated – Always carry water, especially on long rides. Hydration is key to maintaining your energy levels.
  4. Be Safe – Wear a helmet, and make sure your bike is in good working condition before every ride.

As for gear, I’ve found that a reliable bike, comfortable clothes, and a good pair of gloves are essential for any ride. I’ve also been using a fitness tracker called Strava to track my progress, which has been great for setting goals and monitoring my performance.

Where Cycling Is Taking Me

Looking ahead, I’m excited for what the future holds in my cycling journey. There are still so many new trails to explore and challenges to conquer. One of my goals is to ride across different countries, experiencing the world from the seat of my bike.

Cycling has taught me that the journey itself is just as important as the destination. It’s not always about where I’m going, but how I grow and evolve along the way. And I’m excited to see where the road will take me next.

item.title: Why I Love Black Coffee and the Ritual of Brewing It
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
There’s something about black coffee that resonates deeply with me. It’s not just the rich, bold flavor or the caffeine boost—it’s the simplicity and authenticity of it all. Black coffee strips everything down to its essence, allowing me to fully savor the pure taste of the beans. No milk, no sugar—just the unadulterated goodness of coffee.

Every morning, I get to begin my day with a small yet meaningful ritual: making my coffee. I don’t just pour hot water over grounds or press a button on an automatic machine. For me, making coffee is a ceremony. I take the time to enjoy the process, as if the brewing of the coffee itself sets the tone for the day ahead.

The star of this ritual is my Delonghi Espresso machine. The sleek, efficient design and the smoothness of the espresso it brews make every cup feel like a treat. It’s more than just a machine—it’s an extension of my love for the craft of coffee-making. The sound of the machine whirring as it grinds the beans, the aroma that fills the air as the espresso drips into my cup—these small moments are what make the process special.

One of the things that adds a personal touch to my coffee is the beans I use. Currently, my favorite is Batangas coffee. I get it from one of the women in our church who often travels to Batangas. We call it "pasabuy," a Filipino term for items bought by someone for friends or family as a gesture of care. This Batangas coffee has a rich, smooth flavor that perfectly complements the espresso brewing process. It’s not just about the taste—it’s the connection I feel to the people I know who bring it to me, making each cup more than just a drink, but a part of my community and my morning routine.

I also love the adventure of discovering new places with the perfect cup of black coffee. Sometimes, I get on my bike and cycle to different spots, searching for that ideal brew. It’s a fun way to combine my love for cycling with my passion for coffee. Each new place offers a different experience—whether it’s a cozy local café, a hidden gem with an unmatched atmosphere, or a barista who takes their coffee seriously. The thrill of finding that perfect cup makes the journey all the more rewarding.

I love the control I have over every step, from choosing the beans to adjusting the grind size, the water temperature, and the brewing time. Each cup is a reflection of my choices, a reminder that I’m not just drinking coffee—I’m crafting it.

As I sip my black coffee in the quiet morning hours or after a refreshing bike ride, I’m reminded of the simplicity and mindfulness that this ritual brings into my life. It’s a moment of pause before the busyness of the day begins, a chance to center myself. Whether it’s the steady rhythm of the espresso machine or the first satisfying sip, there’s something deeply comforting about making and enjoying a perfect cup of black coffee. It’s my way of starting the day on the right note, every single morning.

item.title: Why I Cycle in Every Country I Travel
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
Traveling is an experience that enriches the soul and broadens the mind. As someone who loves to explore the world, I’ve found that cycling has become the perfect way for me to connect with the places I visit. It’s not just about getting from one point to another, it’s about embracing the journey, discovering new cultures, and experiencing life at a different pace. Here’s why cycling has become a must-do activity in every country I travel to.

1. A Deeper Connection to the Place

When I cycle through a city or rural area, I’m not just passing by—it’s a slow, intimate experience. You notice the small details that you would miss in a car or bus: the scent of freshly baked bread from a corner bakery, the sound of locals chatting over coffee, or the wind rustling through the trees in a park. Cycling allows me to move at a pace that connects me with the rhythm of a place, rather than just observing it from a distance.

2. The Freedom of Exploration

Cycling gives me the freedom to go off the beaten path. While buses and taxis are confined to specific routes, my bike can take me down quiet alleys, to hidden beaches, or into the heart of a local neighborhood. It allows me to create my own adventure and find gems that might not appear in any travel guide. Whether it’s a secluded mountain trail or a charming street lined with local art shops, my bike is the key to unlock places only the locals know.

3. A Sustainable Way to Travel

As someone who values sustainability, cycling aligns perfectly with my travel ethos. It’s an eco-friendly way to explore, reducing my carbon footprint while still being able to experience the world in all its glory. I believe that travel doesn’t have to come at the expense of the environment, and cycling allows me to explore new destinations with minimal impact.

4. The Joy of Physical Challenge

Cycling is more than just a means of transportation; it’s also a form of self-expression and challenge. Whether I'm climbing the hills of a mountain pass or navigating busy city streets, the physical exertion of cycling makes me feel alive. It’s an opportunity to push my limits and discover what my body is capable of. Plus, cycling helps me stay active, so I can enjoy local cuisine without worrying too much about overindulgence!

5. A Unique Perspective

I’ve found that cycling gives me a unique perspective on the places I visit. It’s not just about the landmarks, but the journey in between. Cycling helps me see the contrasts of a place, like the bustling energy of a city center versus the quiet serenity of the countryside. These differences tell the true story of a destination, and cycling allows me to experience them firsthand.

7. Cycling is Part of My Journey

Lastly, cycling is more than just an activity—it’s a part of who I am. It’s a reflection of my values and passions. For me, every bike ride is a personal journey, one that aligns with my love for exploration, self-growth, and my deep faith in Jesus. It’s a reminder that life is not just about where you’re going but how you get there.

Traveling by bike allows me to see the world through a different lens, and that’s why I cycle in every country I visit.

What about you? Do you find unique ways to connect with the places you travel to? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

item.title: Where Shuttles Fly and Relationships Thrive
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
Every weekend, my life takes on a rhythm of movement, laughter, and shared energy as I step onto the badminton court. It's not just about the game—it’s about the moments spent with people who matter to me.

A Weekend Ritual

Saturday or Sunday afternoons are reserved for this special gathering. The court becomes a melting pot of friends, churchmates, and my girlfriend’s family. It’s a tradition now—a way to unwind, stay fit, and share quality time.

The Game

Badminton is more than just a sport; it’s a test of agility, focus, and teamwork. The quick exchanges, smashing rallies, and occasional playful banter make every match exciting. Some of us play with intensity, aiming for every corner of the court, while others join for fun, bringing light-heartedness to the game.

Strengthening Bonds

What I love most is how this shared activity strengthens relationships. My friends and I cheer each other on, my churchmates bring a sense of fellowship, and playing alongside my girlfriend’s family creates a bond like no other. We’re not just playing; we’re building memories that will last a lifetime.

Post-Match Moments

After the games, we often sit down to catch our breath and share stories. Sometimes, we grab food or coffee nearby, extending the joy of togetherness. These post-game moments are as special as the games themselves—a time to connect and reflect.

Why It Matters

Badminton every weekend isn’t just a hobby for me. It’s a chance to stay active, nurture relationships, and create a space where everyone feels part of something bigger. It reminds me that life’s simplest joys often come from shared experiences.

Whether I’m smashing shuttles or sharing laughs, these weekends are a highlight of my week—a testament to the power of community, family, and the little traditions that make life rich.

item.title: The Lord is My Shepherd
item.dc:creator: jhimross
item.content:encoded:
In the hustle and bustle of life, it’s easy to feel lost, overwhelmed, or even fearful. Amid these challenges, Psalm 23 stands as a timeless reminder of God’s faithful provision, protection, and presence. This psalm, written by King David, is more than just beautiful poetry—it’s a lifeline for our faith and a beacon of hope.

The Shepherd Who Provides

"The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want."


David opens Psalm 23 with a profound declaration: God is our shepherd, and as such, He meets all our needs. This is a promise of sufficiency—not necessarily that we’ll have everything we desire, but that we’ll have everything we truly need.

As someone who loves cycling, I often find parallels between this verse and my journey on the road. When I cycle, I bring only the essentials, trusting that what I carry is enough to sustain me. In life, God ensures we lack nothing of eternal significance, reminding us to trust in His perfect provision.

Rest for the Weary

"He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul."
Have you ever experienced moments when your soul feels burdened? For me, weekends of badminton with friends and family or a quiet morning ritual of making black coffee help refresh my spirit. Psalm 23 tells us that God provides even greater rest—not just for our bodies but for our souls.

The imagery of green pastures and still waters paints a picture of peace and restoration. In a world that glorifies busyness, God calls us to slow down and rest in Him, trusting that He is the one who restores what is broken and weary within us.

Guidance on the Path

"He leads me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake."
Life can feel like a winding trail, filled with forks and decisions that leave us unsure of the right direction. As someone who navigates both the literal roads on a bike and the figurative roads of life, this verse reassures me that God is our perfect guide.

He leads us, not for our glory, but for His. And when we choose to follow Him, we’re walking in paths that honor His name and fulfill His purpose for our lives.

"Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me."
Dark valleys are inevitable. Whether it’s facing uncertainty, grief, or personal struggles, we’ve all experienced moments that feel overwhelming. In these valleys, David reminds us that we’re never alone.

God’s presence is constant, and His tools—like the shepherd’s rod and staff—are symbols of His protection and guidance. For me, this assurance brings courage, much like the way I rely on my faith to push through tough climbs during a cycling route.

Overflowing Blessings

"You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows."
God’s blessings aren’t limited by our circumstances. Even in the face of opposition or hardship, He lavishes us with His goodness. This verse is a vivid reminder that His provision isn’t just enough—it’s abundant.

When I sip a perfect cup of Batangas coffee or share joyful moments with loved ones, I see glimpses of this overflowing cup—a life touched by God’s grace in the simplest of joys.

The Pursuit of Love

"Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I shall dwell in the house of the Lord forever."
This final verse brings it all together. God’s goodness and mercy are not passive; they actively pursue us every day of our lives. Our ultimate hope is dwelling with Him forever—a promise that gives meaning to every moment we live.

Psalm 23 is an Invitation


Psalm 23 is more than a psalm to read—it’s a psalm to live. It’s a call to trust the Shepherd who provides, leads, protects, and blesses.

As I journey through life—on my bike, in my faith, and in my relationships—I’m continually reminded of God’s unchanging faithfulness. Whether you're cycling through smooth roads or climbing steep hills, let Psalm 23 be your anthem of trust and peace.

What about you? How has Psalm 23 spoken to your heart? Share your reflections—I’d love to hear them!
